{"body":"Part of #35 (section 3, enhancement 3).

## The picture

At 3x zoom, one art pixel should be a crisp 3x3 block. The renderer computes `screen = (world − camera) × zoom` — so if the camera eases to x = 100.4, even a perfectly integer-positioned sprite lands fractionally, and its pixels split across screen-pixel boundaries: this column renders 2px wide, the next 4px, shifting as the camera glides. The player sees the whole world **shimmer and crawl** whenever the camera moves. Maddening to debug, because every individual thing checks out — art 1:1, sprites snapped, zoom integer. The camera is the coordinate nobody checked.

Upstream already has two-thirds of the answer: `SpritePrepSystem(pixelPerfectRendering:)` and its text sibling snap POSITIONS. But snapping sprites while the camera stays fractional just moves the fraction — the subtraction reintroduces it. *Witch v Necromancer* proved it by measuring exact-colour run lengths across screenshots (all must be multiples of the zoom); they were not, until the camera snapped too.

## Two legitimate styles — this flag serves one and must not foreclose the other

**Fractional camera movement over pixel art is a valid aesthetic, not a defect.** The premise this PR documents is a fork, not a mandate:

1. **Hard-snap retro** — every art pixel is an exact NxN screen block at all times. Requires ALL THREE snaps: integer scale, snapped positions (sprite + text), snapped camera. This flag is the missing third.
2. **Smooth-scroll pixel art** — the world renders crisp on the virtual-pixel grid, but the CAMERA moves freely at output resolution: the composed frame is displaced by the sub-virtual-pixel remainder at composite time, and border pixels get cut. Buttery movement, crisp pixels. This style KEEPS the camera fractional — `pixelSnap` stays off — and applies the remainder at the final blit (a screen-composition concern, outside this system).

The broken look lives only in the halfway mix: a fractional camera with the zoom applied inside the view transform, so art is **sampled** at fractional positions. Pick a style; be consistent.

view matrix every frame — so it lives at `MonoDreams/rendering/Camera.cs`, not in

guarantee). Toggle `IsActive` to switch the tracked target.

The reference pipeline places `CameraFollowSystem` after the physics / movement

target) eases smoothly back inside rather than snapping to the edge. When null
the camera follows freely.

single smooth easing path to an in-bounds goal.

## What

`CameraSyncSystem` gains one defaulted ctor param — `pixelSnap = false`. When set, the camera entity's eased `WorldPosition` is rounded to whole world pixels (`MathF.Round`) on its way to the `Camera` adapter. Ported from the proven reference in `roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj`.

- **Opt-in:** default `false`; every existing call site is untouched and the adapter copy is bit-exact — existing games render byte-identical (covered by `Default_NoSnap_AdapterEqualsEntityPositionExactly`).
- **The snap lives on the adapter COPY only** — the camera entity's eased/authored position stays smooth and fractional, so follow easing is unaffected and the saved/inspected value never drifts. Rotation and zoom flow through unrounded.

## Premise (the fork, not a mandate)

New camera premise: *"`pixelSnap` is one of two first-class pixel-art styles — the failure mode is the mix"*:

1. **Hard-snap retro** — ALL THREE snaps: integer zoom, snapped sprite+text positions (`SpritePrepSystem`/`TextPrepSystem` `pixelPerfectRendering`), snapped camera (this flag). Every art pixel is an exact NxN screen block.
2. **Smooth-scroll pixel art** — camera stays fractional (`pixelSnap` off), the composed frame is displaced by the sub-virtual-pixel remainder at composite time (outside this system). Buttery movement, crisp pixels.

The broken shimmer/crawl look lives only in the halfway mix — a fractional camera with the zoom applied inside the view transform. Fine print for shakes (learned in the game): round the offsets (an unrounded shake smears the whole screen in style 1) and remove last frame's offset before applying the next (or the shake permanently displaces the camera) — consistent with the existing "shake runs AFTER the sync, never feeds back into the entity" clause.
